subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw expose host IPC for Docker sandboxes, and if yes should it be a narrow `sandbox.docker.ipc` break-glass field instead of generic raw Docker argument passthrough?
rationale: The remaining request changes the sandbox isolation boundary and public config contract; source evidence shows GPU passthrough is solved, but host IPC/raw args are not a routine bug fix.

options.title: Add narrow IPC break-glass field
options.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with validation, docs, config hashing, Docker create-args support, security-audit coverage, and focused tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

options.title: Reject host IPC in core
options.body: Document GPU passthrough as the supported high-power Docker path and keep host IPC unavailable because it weakens sandbox isolation.

options.title: Define namespace policy first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, capabilities, and other dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Add narrow IPC break-glass field
recommendation.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with validation, docs, config hashing, Docker create-args support, security-audit coverage, and focused tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest policy-history signal for namespace-sharing sandbox hardening is the Docker namespace-join and dangerous-override work connected to this path.
